\[
\theta_s = \theta + \phi + s\, e^{-\rho / (R \ln 2 / 5)},
\quad \rho_s = \rho,
\qquad s = 3,\ R = 120,\ \phi = 0^{\circ}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(\rho, \theta\): The polar coordinates around the image center
- \(s\): The strength, the turn at the center in radians
- \(R\): The radius
- \(\phi\): The rotation added everywhere

rho and theta are the polar coordinates of an output pixel around the image center. It reads the source at the same distance, turned by the rotation phi plus s times an exponential decay. With the decay length R ln 2 / 5, the turn at rho = R has fallen by the factor e^(-5 / ln 2), about 0.0007, as scikit-image intends. This is the mapping of scikit-image's transform.swirl. scikit-image puts its default center at (W / 2, H / 2) in pixel indices, half a pixel from the true center. This filter uses the true center ((W - 1) / 2, (H - 1) / 2). Each output pixel reads the source at the mapped position with bilinear interpolation, the inverse mapping of Gonzalez and Woods, so no holes appear.
